description: Tests the scalar-combination reading of the positive half of conj:c1-ggm-bar-parity-faces — that the diagonal Z/2 character (-1)^m is the WHOLE difference. The twist maps the Stokes carrier's recurrence y_{m+2} - (2-q^{m+1})y_{m+1} + y_m = 0 to the sign-flipped one (verified to 1e-50 relative, and proved in Lean as barTwist_recursion), and it inverts EVERY consecutive-pair sign, not only the alternating ones. Since the carrier's solution is flip-free below m+1 = log2/log q, the twisted sequence acquires flips exactly there — measured — and doorV_parity_no_identity needs only one flip. So the twist relocates the parity obstruction rather than removing it. The scalar reading of 'sole residual' is therefore excluded; the module-level reading, where the comparison is up to a gauge, is untouched and remains the conjecture's content.

verdict: The bar-parity twist RELOCATES the parity obstruction, it does not remove it. Proved in Lean (obstruction_fires_on_one_of, twist_clears_only_if_everywhere_alternating) and measured here: the twisted sequence still flips, at exactly the indices where the untwisted one did not. Consequence: 'the diagonal Z/2 character is the sole residual' cannot be read as 'applying the character makes the target a non-negative combination of the squares'. It must be read at the MODULE level, up to a gauge. This does not refute the conjecture — it removes one reading of it, and the block has been amended to say which. Deliberately NOT reported: a scalar fit against a prose-reconstructed f_+/f_-, which would not be trustworthy. Nothing wired to production.
